result:
PR #590 opened: https://github.com/FChecklist/compliance-tracker/pull/590

Summary of what shipped in this increment 2:

- **WebLLM wiring** — real model `Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-q4f16_1-MLC` (verified present in the installed library's own catalog), wired behind a new `shouldAttemptWebLlm` gate in `tier-orchestrator.ts`, with tests proving it's reachable and falls back honestly when WebGPU is absent.
- **engine-browser-mcp + engine-browser-function** — a real JSON-RPC-shaped tool-calling contract (`tool-calling.ts`) with genuine register→call→execute round trips.
- **engine-browser-worker deepening** — a `SharedArrayBuffer`/`Atomics`-coordinated worker pool, tested against real Bun `Worker` instances (not mocked).
- **engine-browser-transformers** — real `Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` embedding pipeline via `@huggingface/transformers`.
- **stack-parallelism deepening** and **tier-local IndexedDB model-weight caching** (native flag for WebLLM, custom cache adapter for Transformers.js).

All 58 new tests pass, full repo suite is 2088/2088, and `tsc`/`eslint` are clean. One honest limitation found and documented: `@huggingface/transformers` can't run under Bun in this sandbox due to a `sharp`/libvips `dlopen` incompatibility (works fine under plain `node`, and irrelevant to the actual browser bundle) — I verified the real model integration via a one-off `node` script before falling back to injected-factory tests for the committed suite.

Item 8 (updating the phase-plan YAML) lives in a separate repo (`claude-control`) not present in this workspace, so I documented it as an explicit cross-repo follow-up rather than guessing at it. The PR is open and awaiting the mandatory audit comment before merge, per this repo's governance rules.
